catalog_quote: The stress and tone system in Godoberi is quite complex. Godoberi contrasts with other languages discussed so far: it possesses word stress in addition to a tonal system. For nominals, several accentual paradigms have been proposed, with fixed and mobile stress (Saidova 1973:36; Kibrik et al. 1996:4). ... the relevant suprasegmental feature has to do with the stiffness and slackness of articulators and/or spectral properties of vowels, and not pitch. Combinations of HH, LL and HL but not LH are attested ... Both H and L can carry stress, but the rules of stress placement have not been established. According to Saidova (1973: 36), stress on the second syllable is most common in Godoberi, as in other Avar-Andic languages, but it is unclear how robust this generalization is for Godoberi. There are stress-based minimal pairs: basá ‘say/sing.IMP’, bása ‘say.PST.3SG.M’: ámi ‘wooden dish’, amí…

tone_statements.citation: Kodzasov, Sandro V. 2003. Towards an evolutionary typology of stress. In M. J. Solé, D. Recasens & J. Romero (eds.), Proceedings of the 15th International Congress of Phonetic Sciences (ICPhS-15), Barcelona, 3-9 August 2003, 63-66. Barcelona: UAB / IPA.
tone_statements.quote: Only three languages (among 14) display pronounced stress. These are Avar which functions as lingua franca of the whole region, Godoberi and Chamalal. ... The position of stress is determined by the distribution of three parametric values: syllabic weight, stiffness/slackness of vocalic articulation (intuitively it is associated by speakers with high and low tones), and the location of a specific impulse of tenseness. In Godoberi the difference of breathy and neutral voice is involved additionally in the positioning of stress and there are nine accentual paradigms in nouns. ... Supposedly, the stiff/slack opposition in these languages goes back to tonal contrasts.

sources.note: Godoberi is one of only three Northern Daghestanian languages with pronounced (lexical, paradigmatic) stress; stress position depends on syllable weight, a stiff/slack vocalic-articulation opposition that speakers intuitively hear as high vs low tone, and a once-per-word 'impulse of tenseness'; in Godoberi breathy vs neutral voice is additionally involved, giving nine noun accentual paradigms, verbs much simpler; the stiff/slack ('H/L') opposition 'supposedly goes back to tonal contrasts', while true syllabic tones are attributed to Akhwakh and Andi, not Godoberi. I.e. a quasi-tonal register…

In this IJaLI/Xalilov series the sketch opens with phonetics (sound inventory, stress), so it most likely restates Godoberi word prosody as (weak, partly mobile) dynamic stress, as in Saidova 1973/2004; a discussion of Kodzasov's stiff/slack H/L register ('tone') is unlikely and not established. Does not supersede the Kodzasov 2003 / Borise 2020 statements listed…
